situation.note: I want to marry Faraz. we've been together 5 years. my parents say they will cut ties. I love them and I love him. I feel I am being asked to choose who I am.

understanding.bridge: The choice they are forcing on you is not a choice between two people. It is a test of whether your own truth can stand against their demand.
understanding.week_thesis: Seven days from being asked to choose between two loves to seeing that the choice is about your own truth, and finding the words to hold it.

week_beats.hook: You recognise being asked to choose between two loves, and the fear of losing the one who raised you.
week_beats.diagnose: You see that the demand is not about but about whether your own truth can stand.

understanding.mirror: The self cannot be cut, burned or made less. What they see is a role, and you were never only a role.
understanding.insight: They are not asking you to choose between two people. They are asking you to choose between their picture of you and your own truth.
understanding.mechanism_label: Being seen as less than you are

queries.hook: Being asked to choose between the people you love most, and feeling that your own identity is the thing on the line.
queries.diagnose: When others see only a role, their picture shows their smallness; the harm deepens only when their picture begins to replace your own.
queries.steady: What you are cannot be cut smaller by what they see; they do not decide your worth, and standing in your own truth is itself the duty.
queries.act: Speak the true thing gently and firmly, hold your ground on what is yours, and do your own duty without shrinking to fit the picture they hold.
queries.story: A woman of learning and standing, dismissed by her husband's family, who questioned them openly and stood in her truth until they had no answer.

verse.speaker: Krishna
verse.setting: Krishna to Arjuna on being your own friend and staying steady in honour and insult.
verse.sanskrit: उद्धरेदात्मनाऽऽत्मानं नात्मानमवसादयेत् । आत्मैव ह्यात्मनो बन्धुरात्मैव रिपुरात्मनः ॥
verse.line: Be on your own side. Lift yourself up, don't push yourself down. You can be your own friend.
verse.translation: Raise yourself by your own self; do not let yourself sink. For the self alone is the friend of the self, and the self alone is the enemy of the self.
verse.why: You can be your own best friend or worst enemy; choose friend.
verse.misuse: Not 'you're alone, so don't ask for help'. Arjuna himself asks for help; this is about not abandoning yourself.

prasang.title: Lift yourself by yourself; marks of the realised
prasang.summary: Raise yourself by yourself; you are your own friend or enemy. The self-mastered person stays calm in heat and cold, praise and blame, and sees friend and foe alike.
prasang.lesson: You can be your own best friend or worst enemy; choose friend.

verse.meaning: Krishna tells Arjuna that he alone is his own best friend and his own worst enemy. Arjuna has laid down his weapons and refused to fight. He is caught between his love for his family and his duty as a warrior. Krishna says do not let yourself sink into this despair. You could raise yourself up. You are the only one who can do it. You can be your own friend, or you can be your own enemy. The choice is yours.
verse.for_you: What you are cannot be cut smaller by what they see; your worth was never theirs to grant, and standing in your own truth is itself the duty.
verse.try_today: Notice one moment today when you choose your own truth over their demand.
verse.scene_line: You are on the battlefield of a choice between two loves.
asks: How do I stand by my truth without losing my family?
What does it mean to be my own best friend?
How do I raise myself up when they push me down?

verse.speaker: Bhishma
verse.setting: Bhishma on public slander, answering Yudhishthira's question about being insulted in an assembly.
verse.sanskrit: परिवादं ब्रुवाणो हि दुरात्मा वै महाजने / प्रकाशयति दोषान्स्वान्सर्पः फणमिवोन्नतम्
verse.line: Whoever runs others down in public only puts their own faults on display.
verse.translation: The person who speaks ill of others in front of a crowd only puts his own faults on display, the way a snake raises its hood.
verse.why: Careless critics show their own faults. Let their words pass like a crow's cawing.

prasang.title: Bhishma on bearing slander
prasang.summary: Yudhishthira asks how to respond when a harsh fool abuses you in public. Bhishma: let it pass like a crow cawing; the slanderer only displays his own faults.
prasang.lesson: Careless critics show their own faults. Let their words pass like a crow's cawing.

verse.for_you: When others see only a role, their picture is their smallness and not your measure; the harm deepens only when their picture begins to replace your own.

verse.speaker: Yama
verse.setting: Yama on the inner self and the world's pain.
verse.sanskrit: सूर्यो यथा सर्वलोकस्य चक्षुः न लिप्यते चाक्षुषैर्बाह्यदोषैः । एकस्तथा सर्वभूतान्तरात्मा न लिप्यते लोकदुःखेन बाह्यः ॥
verse.line: The sun shows every flaw yet stays untouched. Your deepest self stays untouched by the world's sorrow.
verse.translation: Just as the sun, the eye of the whole world, is not stained by the flaws the eyes see outside, so the one inner self of all beings is not stained by the sorrow of the world; it stands apart.
verse.why: Look inward; what lasts is not out there among passing things.

prasang.title: Turning the gaze inward
prasang.summary: In the second half of his teaching, Yama explains that our senses face outward, so we miss what is within. The wise turn inward and stop looking for lasting things among passing ones; when the knots of the heart are cut, a person is free.
prasang.lesson: Look inward; what lasts is not out there among passing things.

verse.meaning: Yama is teaching Nachiketa about the inner self. The sun is the eye of the world. It shines on everything and reveals every flaw. But the sun itself is never stained by what it sees. In the same way, your deepest self is the one inner self in all beings. It is never stained by the sorrow of the world. It stands apart. The teaching says to turn your gaze inward. Stop looking for what lasts out there among passing things. When you look within, the knots of the heart are cut.
verse.for_you: They are making your faith seem like a flaw in the room. But your inner truth is like the sun. It stays untouched by the noise of their demand. You do not need to lower yourself to fit their picture. Your own truth is the one that lasts.
verse.try_today: Notice one moment today when you feel your truth is being questioned.

verse.speaker: Teacher
verse.setting: Rules of conduct for a renunciant.
verse.sanskrit: नात्यर्थं सुखदुःखाभ्यां शरीरमुपतायेत् । स्तूयमानो न तुषेत निन्दितो न शपेत्परान् ॥
verse.line: Don't wear out your body chasing pleasure or fleeing pain. Praised, don't gloat; blamed, don't curse others.
verse.translation: Let him not torment the body too much for the sake of pleasure or pain. Praised, let him not gloat; blamed, let him not curse others.
verse.meaning: A teacher is laying out the rules for someone who has stepped away from ordinary life. The teacher says do not wear out your body chasing pleasure or fleeing pain. When people praise you, do not gloat. When they blame you, do not curse them back.
verse.for_you: Someone is trying to make your faith feel like a flaw, and they want you to feel small for holding it. Your body is carrying that pressure. Stay on your own side. You do not have to wear yourself out to prove you are right.
verse.try_today: Notice when you start to shrink and stop.
verse.scene_line: You stand in the middle of a room where the walls are closing in.
asks: How do I stop myself from shrinking?
How do I curse back without words?

verse.speaker: Krishna
verse.setting: Krishna on three kinds of food, effort, speech and giving.
verse.sanskrit: अनुद्वेगकरं वाक्यं सत्यं प्रियहितं च यत् । स्वाध्यायाभ्यसनं चैव वाङ्मयं तप उच्यते ॥
verse.line: Speak words that don't wound, that are true, kind and helpful. That is discipline of speech.
verse.translation: Speech that causes no distress, that is truthful, pleasant and beneficial, and the regular study of sacred texts: this is called austerity of speech.
verse.why: Speak kindly and truly, give without strings, and drop the show.
verse.misuse: Kind speech doesn't mean avoiding hard truths; it means saying them without cruelty.

matched.label: I have to give someone bad news

prasang.title: Three kinds of food, offering, austerity and giving
prasang.summary: Food, offering, austerity and giving each come in three kinds. Speech should be true, kind and helpful; giving should expect nothing back; effort for show doesn't last.
prasang.lesson: Speak kindly and truly, give without strings, and drop the show.

verse.meaning: Krishna is telling Arjuna about three kinds of giving. He speaks of those who give with the thought that something will be returned, those who give with the thought that something will be received back, and those who give out of a sense of duty. He says the last kind is the best. The same rule applies to speech. Words that do not cause pain, that are true, pleasant and useful, and that come from a place of discipline, are the highest form of speech. This is not about being nice to avoid a fight.
verse.for_you: The person in your life wants your faith to be a small part of who you are. They want you to hide it, or change it, or pretend it is not there. You do not have to shrink yourself to make their world smaller.
verse.try_today: Notice one moment when you almost hide your own truth. Let the words come out anyway.
verse.scene_line: You are at the table where they ask you to shrink, and you are choosing to speak the full size of yourself.
asks: How do I say no without making them hate me?
What is the difference between hiding and choosing my time?
Can my own truth be a gift to them?

verse.speaker: Teacher
verse.setting: The graduation address as a student leaves to start family life.
verse.sanskrit: वेदमनूच्याचार्योन्तेवासिनमनुशास्ति । सत्यं वद । धर्मं चर । स्वाध्यायान्मा प्रमदः ।
verse.line: Speak the truth. Do what is right. Never stop learning.
verse.translation: Having taught the Veda, the teacher instructs the student: Speak the truth. Practise what is right. Do not neglect your study.
verse.why: Truth, right action, gratitude and graceful giving: a whole life in one speech.

prasang.title: The graduation address
prasang.summary: As a student finishes his studies and leaves to start family life, the teacher gives him parting instructions: speak truth, do right, keep learning, honour mother, father, teacher and guest, give with grace. He even tells the student to copy only the teachers' good conduct, and when in doubt to act as thoughtful, gentle people would.
prasang.lesson: Truth, right action, gratitude and graceful giving: a whole life in one speech.

verse.meaning: A teacher stands at the door as a student leaves to start a family. The teacher speaks the truth about how to live. The teacher says speak the truth. Do what is right. Never stop learning. The teacher means a whole life is held in these three lines. You do not need a grand speech. You need only to speak the truth, do what is right, and keep learning.
verse.for_you: They are asking you to shrink. They want you to choose a smaller version of yourself that fits their comfort. But your truth is not a weapon. It is simply the ground you stand on. You do not have to prove it with anger. You only have to live it.
verse.try_today: Say one true thing aloud that they do not want to hear.
verse.scene_line: You stand at the door they want you to leave, holding the truth they cannot see.
asks: How do I speak truth without breaking the bond?
What if my truth is the only thing I have left?
Can I learn from this pain without letting it own me?

story.title: Parvati holds to her choice
story.story_hook: The sages came to talk Parvati out of it, and they listed every flaw in the man she had chosen.
story.summary: Reborn as Parvati, Sati resolves to marry Shiva and spends years in austerity. The seven sages come to test her, mocking Shiva as a homeless ascetic and offering her a better match. She answers that gold keeps its nature even in fire, and that the heart wants the one it has chosen.
story.lesson: Persistence is choosing the same thing again each day, even when others call it foolish.

anchor.speaker: Parvati
anchor.setting: Parvati answers the sages who mock her resolve to win Shiva through years of austerity.
anchor.sanskrit: सत्य कहेहु गिरिभव तनु एहा। हठ न छूट छूटै बरु देहा॥ कनकउ पुनि पषान तें होई। जारेहुँ सहजु न परिहर सोई ॥
anchor.line: Gold comes from stone, and even in fire it stays gold. Hold to what you are.
anchor.translation: You speak truly: this body was born of a mountain, so its resolve will not break, even if the body does. Gold too is born of stone, and even in fire it does not give up its nature.
anchor.why: Persistence is choosing the same thing again each day, even when others call it foolish.
anchor.misuse: Steadiness is not stubbornness; keep checking that the goal is still worth it.

prasang.title: Parvati holds to her choice
prasang.summary: Reborn as Parvati, Sati resolves to marry Shiva and spends years in austerity. The seven sages come to test her, mocking Shiva as a homeless ascetic and offering her a better match. She answers that gold keeps its nature even in fire, and that the heart wants the one it has chosen.
prasang.story_hook: The sages came to talk Parvati out of it, and they listed every flaw in the man she had chosen.
prasang.lesson: Persistence is choosing the same thing again each day, even when others call it foolish.

story.hook_title: The sages listed every flaw in the man Parvati had chosen
story.teaser: The sages listed every flaw in the man Parvati had chosen
asks: How do I keep my heart steady when they keep changing the story?
What does it mean to hold to my choice when it costs me peace?
How do I know if my truth is real or just stubbornness?
